recommendation_reason: Use the maintained tokio-rusqlite bridge behind the core storage module. Both native async stacks were comparable; the bridge preserves the current supported opening guard without a fork. Both delegate connection workers. Keep admission, fairness, durable outcomes and physical completion with their Rust owners; qualify larger grouping and real provider-output backpressure in implementation.

Group64 diagnostic · ONE heavy run per stack
Group64 diagnostic p95 · not repeated capacity qualification
Observed threads · one writer / two readers

limits: 24 original 30-second windows (20 measured) plus two single diagnostic windows; no production migration.
Both original heavy stacks rejected offered output. Larger groups improved the single diagnostic; hot-workspace rejections remain.
Different SQLite engine versions and statement-cache settings; no isolated driver-overhead or universal capacity claim.
Synthetic parent/child streams and transaction shapes; no provider turn mapping, real child execution or GitHub/Jira workflow qualification.
Dropped-reply evidence retained its async owner; arbitrary owner abort/panic and cancelled COMMIT remain unqualified.
Post-window payload audits differ, so whole-process RSS is not a steady-state driver comparison.
No application unit/build/desktop/provider qualification or power-loss/long-soak proof. Future ideas remain probes, not feature commitments.
